edges.description: Sperm are fully immotile, and the mouse also has a sharp fall in sperm number that is far more severe than in patients, where the count is variable and at most mild to moderate.
edges.limitations: Epididymal sperm count falls to about 2% of wild type in the knockout, whereas in patients the count is variable: normal in one cohort and mildly to moderately reduced (2.8-8.0 x10^6/ml) in three patients of another. The mouse therefore has a far more severe spermatogenic defect than any reported human case.

nodes.description: In Dnah12-/- mice, elongating spermatids have an abnormal manchette and misshapen heads, and more seminiferous tubules contain apoptotic cells. This is the only proposed route to the sperm head abnormality. It has been shown only in mice, and how loss of an axonemal dynein disturbs the manchette is unknown.

nodes.description: Dnah12-/- males are infertile, with completely immotile sperm and axonemal defects. Females and their motile cilia are normal. A knock-in model carrying a patient missense variant (Dnah12mut/mut) reproduced the same reproductive defects.

Without DNAH12, the inner-arm heavy chain DNAH1 and the light intermediate chain DNALI1 are missing from sperm flagella. Patient sperm also lose the radial spoke head protein RSPH9 and the central-pair protein SPAG6.

nodes.description: ICSI bypasses the defect. The lesion affects flagellar motility and form, not the sperm nucleus, and the acrosome and head markers are preserved. Fertilization and embryo development after ICSI are reported in patients from three studies and in knockout mice. Numbers are small: in one three-couple series, one couple had a live birth, one a clinical pregnancy, and one was still awaiting embryo transfer.
